- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive (sentiment > 0.3) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or neutral (sentiment < 0.2) — model fails to recognize downward pressure.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overreacts to short-term volatility, then overcorrects in subsequent periods.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in price correction — model often misses the true trend by 1–3 days, especially after sentiment shifts.
- When sentiment is high and price is rising, model forecasts a steeper slope than actual — overestimates momentum.
- When sentiment is low and price is falling, model underestimates the drop — fails to capture sentiment-driven sell-off.
- Correct for sentiment-driven momentum: if sentiment > 0.4, reduce forecast slope; if sentiment < 0.2, increase downward bias.
- Avoid overfitting to recent highs — model often assumes continuation of recent trend, ignoring mean reversion signals.
